tasks.label: shojiwm: install typescript (rollback)
tasks.detail: dist/install.sh --dev --no-config without --rust-config: puts the TypeScript-config build back in place of the Rust config. It writes over the minkade package's /usr/bin/shoji_wm link, so pacman will report that file as changed until the package is reinstalled; going back to an older minkade with `pacman -U` from its cache is the usual way back now. It replaces all of /usr/lib/shojiwm, so the fallbacks there (shoji_wm.previous, shoji_wm.typescript) are removed. Builds release-fast, then asks for sudo. Takes effect at the next session start; uncomment SHOJI_CONFIG in shojiwm-env.fish first. Runs in a memory-bounded transient scope (see 'build limits' below).

tasks.label: minka: build (release-fast)
tasks.detail: cargo build --profile release-fast -p minka: MinkaDE's one binary (minka/), with the compositor, its portal, xwayland-satellite, MinkaShell, MinkaMon and its sampler, MinkaFX, MinkaShot's screenshot commands, MinkaSyu, MinkaThermal, MinkaLedger's core, bartizan-lsp and keysend in it, into target/release-fast/minka. No LTO and incremental, so an edit relinks in seconds. Nothing in the session changes: it runs the installed package. To try this build, run an app from it (`target/release-fast/minka minkamon`), or start the shell or MinkaMon through their launchers with MINKA_BIN set to it. AntiWebUI has no step of its own: the apps compile the submodule's working tree, uncommitted changes included.
tasks.command: systemd-run --user --scope -q --collect -p MemoryHigh=6G -p MemoryMax=10G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -- cargo build --profile release-fast -p minka

tasks.label: minkade: publish package
tasks.detail: minkarepo publish minkade: builds MinkaPKG/minkade (minka in the release profile, thin LTO over everything, then packaging/stage-usr.sh) and adds it to the [minka] repository. Install it with MinkaSyu or `sudo pacman -Syu`: the compositor and the portal change at the next session start, the other apps when they are restarted. A rebuild of an unchanged commit needs a pkgrel bump in the PKGBUILD first (or `minkarepo update minkade`). The previous package stays in pacman's cache, so `pacman -U` with it is the way back.
tasks.command: systemd-run --user --scope -q --collect -p MemoryHigh=6G -p MemoryMax=10G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -- minkarepo publish minkade

tasks.label: floorp: build and install package from local clones
tasks.detail: Builds the Arch package in MinkaPKG/floorp from the committed HEADs of floorp/Floorp, floorp/Floorp-Runtime and floorp/Floorp-core, then installs it with makepkg --install (pacman asks for sudo after the build). The helper refuses dirty clones because makepkg's Git sources cannot see uncommitted changes. This is the full from-source/PGO package build. Runs in a memory-bounded transient scope (see 'build limits' below).

tasks.label: build limits (reference, does nothing)
tasks.detail: Every build task above runs as `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryHigh=6G -p MemoryMax=10G -p MemorySwapMax=2G` with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6. MemoryHigh throttles by reclaim (the build slows, it does not die); MemoryMax is the backstop and DOES kill inside the scope, so a build that dies with a bare 'signal: 9, SIGKILL' hit 10G — raise it here, do not raise it globally. MemorySwapMax IS LOAD-BEARING and must never be dropped: MemoryMax bounds RESIDENT memory only, so without a swap cap a build simply spills into swap, exhausts the system's swap headroom and triggers a GLOBAL OOM that kills your browser and editor instead of the build. That is exactly what happened to the Floorp build on 7/9/2026 — 9.3 GiB resident stayed under a 13 GiB MemoryMax while 9.6 GiB went to swap unbounded. 6 of 8 jobs leaves the desktop two cores and cuts peak RSS, which scales with concurrent rustc. Rationale: 6/9/2026, a release-fast build on top of an 8G lspmux/rust-analyzer set off a four-minute kernel OOM storm (13 kills, none of them the build) that took out Code, GitKraken and the portals. Bounding the build keeps the kill inside the build's own cgroup.
